court: Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit

issues.label: Substantial evidence for fitness determination
issues.why: Court must determine whether the Board's finding that Qoye was fit for duty is supported by substantial evidence.

issues.label: Whether Board considered relevant factors
issues.why: A decision failing to consider relevant factors like VA narcolepsy findings may be arbitrary and capricious.

issues.label: Standard of review application
issues.why: Court must apply the arbitrary/capricious/contrary-to-law/substantial-evidence standard correctly.

issues.label: Weight given to post-service VA disability rating
issues.why: The VA's 40% narcolepsy rating effective at discharge must be reconciled with the Board's fitness finding.

issues.label: Fitness standard: interference with duties
issues.why: Whether narcolepsy significantly interfered with duties at time of separation is the governing legal test.

issues.label: Applicability of liberal consideration
issues.why: Board held liberal consideration inapplicable due to honorable discharge; correctness of that legal conclusion is disputed.

issues.label: Timeliness/statute of limitations on recoupment claim
issues.why: Court found bonus recoupment claim time-barred under the six-year Tucker Act limitations period.

issues.label: Timeliness of record-correction claim
issues.why: Court found record-correction claim time-barred, raising accrual and limitations questions.

issues.label: Claim accrual date determination
issues.why: When the disability-retirement and correction claims accrued affects timeliness analysis.

issues.label: Continuing-claim or accrual-suspension doctrines
issues.why: Whether exhaustion through the Board tolls or suspends the limitations period must be assessed.

issues.label: Failure to convene MEB/PEB during service
issues.why: Navy's failure to diagnose and refer to MEB/PEB bears on whether the disability process was proper.

issues.label: Validity of post hoc informal PEB
issues.why: The retroactive PEB fitness determination's legitimacy and reliance on wrong records must be evaluated.

issues.label: PEB reliance on wrong service member's records
issues.why: Initial use of another member's records raises reliability concerns about the corrected determination.

issues.label: Basis for NEC removal characterization
issues.why: Whether NEC was removed for misconduct or should be medically unfit is expressly disputed.

issues.label: Relationship between NJP misconduct and narcolepsy
issues.why: Whether falsifying maintenance logs is explained/mitigated by narcolepsy affects the NEC characterization.

issues.label: Dispute over whether NEC removal occurred
issues.why: There is factual dispute whether NEC was actually removed in April 2011.

issues.label: Entitlement to disability retirement pay
issues.why: PDRL placement and retirement back pay depend on establishing unfitness for duty.

issues.label: Recoupment bonus refund entitlement
issues.why: Whether recoupment was proper turns on reason for failure to complete the enlistment term.

issues.label: Scope of remand compliance
issues.why: Whether the Board addressed all issues and claims as directed on remand must be verified.

issues.label: Jurisdiction over non-monetary correction claims
issues.why: Court of Federal Claims Tucker Act jurisdiction over record-correction and NEC claims must be established.

issues.label: Money-mandating statute for disability retirement
issues.why: Tucker Act jurisdiction requires a money-mandating source such as 10 U.S.C. disability retirement statutes.

issues.label: De novo review adequacy on remand
issues.why: Whether the Board's April 2022 de novo review was genuinely independent and reasoned.

issues.label: Effect of performance evaluations as evidence
issues.why: Reliance on evaluations not reflecting fatigue must be weighed against contrary witness testimony.

issues.label: Relevance of 2015 mechanic application
issues.why: Post-service job application's probative value for in-service fitness must be assessed.

issues.label: Failure to test for narcolepsy during service
issues.why: Navy's failure to conduct a narcolepsy-specific test bears on the fairness of the fitness determination.

issues.label: Standard for motion to dismiss versus judgment on record
issues.why: Court must apply correct procedural standards distinguishing dismissal from administrative-record judgment.

issues.label: Weight of treating VA physician's opinion
issues.why: The doctor's statement that narcolepsy developed or worsened in service may be a relevant overlooked factor.
